set: B: motion, the way in, the way out, four sheets of consecutive frames at hits on the arrow (1:33.25 to 1:46.32), two at moments of the ball (1:39.00 and 1:42.62), the page turn that ends the page and the slab seating

issues.where: the round black seal/button, all twelve frames (1:45.67 to 1:46.03)
issues.what: the cursor drops into the seal and rocks to a stop with a nicely decaying oscillation, but the seal itself never answers: the black face does not depress, flash, ring or ripple on the frame the cursor lands in it, and the chrome bezel stays frozen. Only the moving thing reacts; the struck thing and the page around it stay mute, so the catch reads half-finished.
issues.fix: on the landing frame, give the button a press: the black face dips 1-2 px and springs back, or a ring flash/ripple in the bezel, timed with the first frame of the cursor's rock

issues.where: the top of the orange rail, 1:42.67 to 1:42.73
issues.what: the ball rolls along the orange rail at a moderate even pace, then between 1:42.67 and 1:42.70 it is suddenly at full flight speed crossing the whole frame in two frames, with nothing visibly causing it: the rail end does not kick, flash or deflect, and there is no hit frame like the red ring flash in set-B-03. The unmotivated jump in speed is the one moment in these sheets that reads as moved by hand rather than loose in a machine.
issues.fix: add a cause on the launch frame: the rail end flicks or a kicker lamp flashes as the ball leaves, matching the contact reactions used at the other hits

issues.where: left and above the ball, 1:38.87 to 1:39.00
issues.what: the ball's trail renders as two or three discrete semi-transparent duplicate balls instead of continuous motion blur; on a still it reads as ghosting/doubling round the ball while the pace along the wire rail is otherwise even and a touch gliding.
issues.fix: render the trail as continuous blur or a single smeared streak, and check the ball's speed along the rail against a steel ball on that slope

issues.what: the slab rotates roughly 90 degrees in about a quarter of a second, which is a little fast and light for a heavy slab; the wind-up (button press at 1:48.40) and the long hold after (settle through 1:49.80, with the seating jiggle visible in set-B-10) carry most of the weight, so the mid-flight lightness is only just noticeable.
issues.fix: steal 2-3 frames from the hold after the turn and give them to the rotation, easing out of the flip so the slab's mass reads during the turn, not only at landing

issues.what: mid-way-in there is a beat where a translucent rectangular panel floats over the dark machine with the blue backglass grid behind it; read left to right it is the one frame in the way-in where you cannot quite tell what you are passing through without the caption.
issues.fix: clarify the transition through the glass: fade the UI panel out fully before the machine interior appears, or hold the dive continuous so no floating semi-transparent panel state is shown
